summary: Takamichi Fukita specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Taisho and Bukkyo Universities under Shozen Kumoi and Yuichi Kajiyama, with postdoctoral mentoring by Heinz Bechert, and served as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1999, 2013).

Takanobu Takahashi (b. 1951) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Madurai Kamaraj University under Rama. Periakaruppan, and Utrecht University (PhD 1988), later teaching at International Buddhist University and the University of Tokyo.

Takanori Kimura (b. 1947) specializes in Buddhist studies and studied at Komazawa University. He served as a lecturer at Yamaguchi University (attested 1996) and head priest at Kaichōji (attested 2003).

Takanori Shintani (b. 1948) works in religious studies, Japanology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Waseda University (~1968–1977) and held posts at the Graduate University for Advanced Studies (~1996–2010) and Kokugakuin University (~2010).

Takanori Unno (b. 1936) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned degrees at Nagoya University under numerous mentors. He held appointments at Nagoya University, Aichi Prefectural University of Fine Arts and Music, and Meijo University (attested 2002).

Takao Hayashi (b. 1949) specializes in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Tohoku, Kyoto, and Brown Universities (PhD 1985 under David Pingree), later serving on the faculty at Doshisha University as assistant professor (1986–1989) and professor (1995–2015).
Takao Kagawa (b. 1926) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Susumu Yamaguchi, Issai Funahashi, and Shoju Inaba, and served as a professor at Bukkyo University.

Takao Maruyama (b. 1929) is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Tohoku University. He held professorships at Rissho University (~1968–~1976), Shinshu University (attested 1983–1984; emeritus ~1988), and Mejiro University (~1988).

Takao Moriyasu (1948–2024) was a historian of Iranian/Central Asian studies and Sinology. Educated at the University of Tokyo and Osaka University, he was an associate professor at Kanazawa and Osaka Universities, later serving as professor at Osaka University (1994–2012).
Takao Suita is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who held appointments as a lecturer at Bukkyo University (attested 1997–2010) and continued affiliation there attested in 2020.

Takao Yamagata (1932–2019) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1952–1960). He served on the faculty at Miyagi Gakuin Women's University (~1972–2003) and chaired the Association for the Study of Indian Religions (attested 1997).
Takashi Hidaka is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a public recruit researcher at the Buddhism and Art Research Center (2012) and as a part-time lecturer at Otani University (attested 2014).

Takashi Iwata (b. 1944) specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Waseda University and the University of Hamburg (Dr. Phil.) under Albrecht Wezler and Lambert Schmithausen, later serving as professor at Waseda University (~1989–2015).
Takashi Koezuka (b. 1939) is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held posts as professor (attested 2001) and professor emeritus (attested 2012) at Osaka University.
Takashi Maeda (b. 1943) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who pursued doctoral studies at Tohoku University. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1995, 2006).

Takashi Nakao (1931–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology, earning degrees from Rissho University and Tokyo University of Education. He taught at Bunkyo University Women's College and served as emeritus professor at Rissho University (1979–2002).

Takashi Ogawa (b. 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University, Peking University, and the University of Tokyo (doctoral degree, 2009), and became an assistant professor at Komazawa University in 1991.
Takashi Yamada (b. 1954) is a scholar in Sinology and religious studies who studied at Hosei University and served as an assistant professor at the Prefectural University of Kumamoto (attested 2003).
Takatoshi Ito (b. 1942) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who served as a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1978–1981, 1991).

Takatoshi Nakamura specializes in Buddhist studies. He studied under Ryukai Mano in 1979 and served as a researcher at the Comprehensive Buddhist Studies Institute at Taisho University (attested 1978).
